title: IPDMA
text:
IPDMA database
OPEN-MRH fills a critical gap left by existing pharmacovigilance and real-world data platforms. This unique infrastructure enables new possibilities for regulatory science, clinical research, and AI-driven safety innovation—ultimately supporting more targeted interventions, reducing preventable hospitalizations and costs, and improving patient safety and health system performance. This project will deliver outputs that directly support key stakeholder needs that will lead to this impact:

Researchers and data scientists will gain access to harmonized, reusable MRH data for pooled analyses and model development across populations. They will be engaged through the co-design workshop, quarterly User Committee meetings, and GitHub-based feedback loops.
Healthcare professionals will benefit from insights generated through platform-supported studies and downstream AI decision support tools (e.g. MRH risk prediction tools). Engagement will include platform design input and tailored dissemination (e.g., publications, presentations and newsletters).
Regulators and pharmacovigilance agencies will use shared metadata and MRH definitions to strengthen surveillance and signal detection. They have participated in the Delphi panel and advisory roles.
AI developers and regulatory bodies will use the regulatory guidance and FAIR data resources co-developed with Utrecht University’s AI Ethics and Law Group to design compliant, trustworthy healthcare AI tools.

title: 2  About
text:
2.1 Motivation
Medication-related harm (MRH) is a major yet under-addressed health challenge, causing approximately 197,000 annual deaths and €79 billion in healthcare costs in the EU alone ((Durand et al. 2024; Hakkarainen et al. 2012; Donaldson et al. 2017)). Despite its importance, MRH research remains limited due to fragmented, inconsistent, and locally restricted datasets, often lacking standardized definitions, interoperability, or secure data sharing infrastructure. The OPEN-MRH project addresses these gaps by developing an internationally accessible, FAIR (Findable, Accessible, Interoperable, Reusable) platform and dataset for clinically adjudicated MRH. By aggregating high-quality datasets, developing consensus-based definitions, and leveraging secure infrastructure, OPEN-MRH will enable reproducible, cross-disciplinary research and support the development of targeted healthcare interventions to prevent MRH—ultimately improving patient outcomes and enhancing the safety of healthcare systems worldwide. OPEN-MRH directly supports the NPOS 2030 Ambition Document by advancing transparency, data reusability, and institutional collaboration, and aligns with the EOSC Multi-Annual Roadmap by delivering scalable, domain-specific infrastructure for real-world health data sharing and reuse.

title: 2  About
text:
2.3 Summary
The OPEN-MRH project will create an open, secure, and interoperable platform for medication-related harm (MRH) research. By harmonizing and pooling de-identified patient-level data from international studies, it will enable large-scale analysis of MRH and its causes. This platform will provide FAIR data, shared standards, and clear guidance for researchers and institutions navigating new EU AI regulations. OPEN-MRH will strengthen global collaboration, support safe use of medications, and promote transparency, reproducibility, and responsible data governance in patient safety research. Eventually, this project will improve patients’ lives and contribute to better and more cost-effective health care by reducing unnecessary MRH in patients.
